first.rationale: I currently intend to simplify onboarding because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding improves time-to-value and SMB activation. I would verify the onboarding and signup records to distinguish where friction is occurring, while checking the pricing record as a competing response to the new entrant. A small guarded test should measure qualified activation, retained usage, and downstream revenue—not completion alone—to avoid trading long-term customer quality for short-term lift.

final.rationale: Run a standard, segmented onboarding-shortening experiment focused on self-serve SMB accounts. The verified result directly improves completion and time-to-value while increasing 30-day retention, addressing both current declines and the sustainable-revenue objective. Use signup simplification only as a secondary diagnostic or holdout comparison because its retention effect was slightly negative. Exclude promotional pricing: despite strong acquisition and qualified-revenue lift, the 12% retention decline indicates poor first-renewal survival. Evaluate activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, renewal-qualified revenue, and guardrails for support burden and abuse.
